title: Razorpay To File UDRHP By Next Week, Eyes IPO By February 2027: Report
summary: Fintech unicorn Razorpay prepares to file updated draft IPO papers targeting a February 2027 launch
detailed: Razorpay is preparing to publicly file its draft IPO papers as early as next week, targeting a February 2027 listing.
The proposed $600 million IPO of fresh shares and an OFS is expected to value the fintech at around $5 billion, down from its $7.5 billion valuation in 2021.
SEBI cleared the company's confidential filing on November 3 following its initial submission in June 2026.
Founded in 2014, Razorpay reported a 65% YoY increase in operating revenue to ₹3,783 Cr in FY25 while expanding into AI-led products like Agent Studio.
sentences: The Bengaluru-based startup is eyeing a potential market debut as early as February 2027, Bloomberg reported, adding that it is expected to begin investor roadshows immediately after the public filing.
Inc42 has reached out to Razorpay for comment on the development.
The story will be updated upon receiving a response.
The report comes within days after the market regulator cleared the ₹6,000 Cr IPO that could potentially value Razorpay at around $5 Bn (₹47,000 Cr).
Pertinent to note that IPO valuation is about 33% lower than the $7.5 Bn valuation it commanded in its last funding round in 2021.
Razorpay had confidentially filed its draft IPO papers in June 2026.
SEBI issued its observations on the company’s filing on November 3, allowing it to proceed with the public issue.
Founded in 2014 by Shashank Kumar and Harshil Mathur, Razorpay offers payment processing, business banking, payroll and lending solutions.
It raised over $800 Mn from investors including Tiger Global Management, Y Combinator, Ribbit Capital and Lightspeed.

The company reported a 65% YoY increase in operating revenue to ₹3,783 Cr in FY25 but slipped into the red, weighed down by ₹1,209 Cr in ESOP expenses and one-time costs linked to its domicile shift from the US to India.
Financial numbers for the period since then would be more apparent when the company files its IPO papers.
Razorpay is also exploring a 0.4% merchant discount rate (MDR) on eligible UPI transactions above ₹2,000 to boost monetisation.
However, its rollout could be delayed until after the 2027 state elections amid concerns over merchant backlash.
The central government, RBI and NPCI are yet to finalise an implementation date, despite much of the regulatory groundwork being complete.
Beyond payments, Razorpay is expanding into AI-led products, including its Agent Studio platform for deploying task-specific AI agents.
The company is looking to tap India’s buoyant IPO market, where firms have raised around $18.6 Bn through initial share sales so far in 2026, nearing last year’s record of $22.4 Bn.
